chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Fitrah (alms of fasting), so he said: Upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, for every person, one Sa' of wheat, or one Sa' of dates, or one Sa' of raisins.

key_terms.صَاع: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What is the required amount and type of food for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Tusi’s al-istibsar, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the universal applicability of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing that the obligation extends to every individual regardless of age, gender, or social status. It specifies the measurement as one Sa' of staple foods such as wheat, dates, or raisins, reflecting the practical economic realities of Medina during the Imams' time. This ruling underscores the principle of social equity, ensuring that even the poorest members of the community contribute to the purification of their fasting.
